subject: ASIN function
notes: PB56 LANDED 2026-08-09 (the Dec-carrier body, standard modes). The returned value - the binary64 Math.Asin approximation, or its SDIDI under a standard mode - lies in [-pi/2, +pi/2] (asin(1) = 1.5707963267948965... < pi/2). kb/Work PB3829 (2026-10-26, owner-approved) RE-DERIVED what this row once claimed: the rule bounds the RETURNED value (the 15.4 temporary), never the value a resultant identifier receives, which 14.9.8.4 r2 hands to 14.6.8, 14.7.4 and 14.7.5. So ASIN(1) ROUNDED into a nine-place receiver stores 1.570796327 (14.7.4.3 r4), past pi/2, and the PB65 clamp that cut it back to 1.570796326 is deleted; the native bare reference now lands exactly as the nested and standard-decimal arms always did. Witnesses: pb65_bounded_returned_value_landing (truncated legs inside the bound, ROUNDED legs past it) and pb3829_rounded_bounded_function_modes (ASIN(+-1) under all nine rounding phrases at scales 4, 2 and -1). retired-witness: conformance:cases/15.10.4-Returned-value-rule/pb65_codomain_clamp (kb/Work PB3829 deleted the codomain clamp (the rule bounds the returned value, not the stored one) and renamed and re-derived its golden) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Intrinsics/CobolIntrinsics.cs#FromDoubleBounded (kb/Work PB3829 deleted the codomain clamp (the rule bounds the returned value, not the stored one) and renamed and re-derived its golden)
